<issue_description>
Converting trailing commas to leading causes unexpected indentation in specific cases
### Search before asking

- [X] I searched the [issues](https://github.com/sqlfluff/sqlfluff/issues) and found no similar issues.


### What Happened

In some cases where SQLFluff is fixing/linting trailing commas to be leading commas within a SELECT statement, the following elements are indented forward for reasons unknown. 

Specifically, this seems to occur when a trailing comma immediately follows an aliased element, and then that element is followed by an empty blank line. For example:

```
SELECT
    acct_id,
    date_x,
    't' AS test,

    CASE
        WHEN condition_1 = '1' THEN ''
        ELSE condition_1
    END AS case_1,

    CASE
        WHEN condition_2 = '2' THEN ''
        ELSE condition_2
    END AS case_2,

    CASE
        WHEN condition_3 = '3' THEN ''
        ELSE condition_3
    END AS case_3,

    closing_date as cls_dt,
    CASE
        WHEN condition_4 = '4' THEN ''
        ELSE condition_4
    END AS case_4,
    dollar_amt,
FROM
    table_x
```

In this example, `'t' AS test,` is followed by an empty line, and then a `CASE` statement. 

### Expected Behaviour

I would expect the configured package to transform the above query into:

```
SELECT
    acct_id
    , date_x
    , 't' AS test

    , CASE
        WHEN condition_1 = '1' THEN ''
        ELSE condition_1
    END AS case_1

    , CASE
        WHEN condition_2 = '2' THEN ''
        ELSE condition_2
    END AS case_2

    , CASE
        WHEN condition_3 = '3' THEN ''
        ELSE condition_3
    END AS case_3

    , closing_date AS cls_dt
    , CASE
        WHEN condition_4 = '4' THEN ''
        ELSE condition_4
    END AS case_4
    , dollar_amt
FROM
    table_x

```

Nothing has changed, except for the commas becoming leading instead of trailing. 

### Observed Behaviour

Instead, this happens:

```
SELECT
    acct_id
    , date_x
    , 't'
        AS test

        , CASE
            WHEN condition_1 = '1' THEN ''
            ELSE condition_1
        END
            AS case_1

            , CASE
                WHEN condition_2 = '2' THEN ''
                ELSE condition_2
            END
                AS case_2

                , CASE
                    WHEN condition_3 = '3' THEN ''
                    ELSE condition_3
                END
                    AS case_3

                    , closing_date AS cls_dt
                    , CASE
                        WHEN condition_4 = '4' THEN ''
                        ELSE condition_4
                    END AS case_4
                    , dollar_amt
                FROM
                    table_x
```

The `AS` statements get forced onto a new line, and each consecutive `CASE` statement is indented forward when following an empty line.
